title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the July 1986 notes (ch. IX/IX bis), a 'magasin' M is a set of abstract 'pieces' (regions or structures) with three relations: a partial order ⊴ (inclusion of pieces), a relation ≪° (presumably 'well inside' / 'interior inclusion'), and a symmetric relation x|0|y ('x and y are disjoint / separated'). An 'atelier' associated to M is a family F ⊂ 𝔓(M) of subsets of M satisfying certain axioms; these subsets behave like 'opens' or 'ideals of pieces', ordered by ≤, ⊆ and ≪. The previous page treats the magasin M(I) of intervals of a totally ordered set I, where 'divisible' means a dense order. On that page the compact structures (points a and closed intervals) are said to be very dense when I is divisible.

This page, Digression 1, defines the direct sum of magasins. Given a family (M_i)_{i∈I}, set M = ⨆ M_i (disjoint union). Take ⊴ and ≪° to be the 'sum' relations, so elements of different summands are never related. Declare x|0|y when x, y lie in different summands, or when they lie in the same M_i and are disjoint there. Grothendieck says checking the axioms is tautological.

Given ateliers F_i on M_i, he defines the sum atelier F = {A ⊂ M | ∀ i, A∩M_i ∈ F_i}. Then F ≅ ∏ F_i, compatibly with the orders ≤, ⊆, ≪.

The purpose is the familiar topological picture: a disjoint union of spaces, whose open sets are the products of the open sets of the pieces. The next page adds two remarks. First, this sum is not obviously a categorical coproduct for the morphisms (gluings) introduced so far, although geometrically it matches the sum of spaces. Second, a magasin should split into connected components for ≪, given a suitable finiteness or existence hypothesis, and unions of distinct components are |0|-disjoint. All of this serves to build an axiomatic, point-free framework for 'spaces of pieces' that is closed under elementary operations.
errors: Slip in the definition of the sum atelier: '∀ i ∈ M_i' should read '∀ i ∈ I'.

≪° is called a 'relation d'ordre somme'. If ≪° is a strict 'well-inside' relation, it is not reflexive, so it is not an order in the strict sense; only 'disjoint union of the relations' is meant. This is harmless.

The isomorphism F ≅ ∏ F_i is asserted without proof. It holds for the set-theoretic map A ↦ (A∩M_i)_i, but compatibility with ≪ depends on how ≪ on ateliers is defined, which is not visible on this page.

ideas.what: Direct sum (disjoint union) of magasins: order relations are taken summandwise, and elements of distinct summands are declared disjoint.
ideas.modern_name: Coproduct / disjoint sum of mereotopological structures (contact algebras, proximity-type structures); disjoint union of spaces in point-free terms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard construction; e.g. products of Boolean contact algebras and frames in point-free topology (Johnstone, Düntsch–Vakarelov, Dimov–Vakarelov)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1986 notes (Montpellier 156-9); the magasin/atelier theory does not appear in Esquisse or Pursuing Stacks as far as known (unsure)

ideas.what: Sum atelier F = {A | A∩M_i ∈ F_i}, with F ≅ ∏ F_i compatibly with the orders.
ideas.modern_name: Frame/locale of opens of a coproduct is the product of the frames

missed.claim: The magasin formalism (pieces with inclusion, well-inside relation ≪ and disjointness |0|, with ateliers as families of pieces) is essentially a mereotopological / contact-algebra or proximity-style axiomatics of space. It was developed independently of the region-based theories of space (Whitehead, de Laguna, Vakarelov) that flourished later. This page only does the routine sum construction, so the point concerns the whole manuscript rather than this page.
missed.quote: x|0|y ⟺ { x∈M_i, y∈M_j, i≠j ou x,y∈M_i, x|0|y au sens de M_i }
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only of historical interest: it shows Grothendieck in 1986 working on a point-free, region-based approach to (likely tame) topology that parallels later mereotopology.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine definition of the direct sum of the author's ad hoc structures, with the standard fact that opens of a disjoint union form a product. Only the broader unpublished magasin/atelier framework is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'magiciens' / 'magicien' should be 'magasins' / 'magasin' (title: 'Somme directe de magasins'), consistent with the next page.
'∀ i∈M_i' is Grothendieck's own slip for '∀ i∈I'; the transcription is faithful to the image.
The last line '[?] multiplicativement [?] les ordres' more likely reads something like '(isomorphisme) compatiblement avec les ordres ≤, ⊆, ≪'.
